title: NASA public AI-use inventory: 2024 inventory — Phase 65 AI for science review
summary: Phase 65 reviews this primary record as part of the AI for science reporting pack. NASA identified active uses spanning autonomous exploration, navigation, science analysis, and mission operations. Active-use labels do not establish comparable benefit, reliability, or safety outcomes.
key_findings: NASA identified active uses spanning autonomous exploration, navigation, science analysis, and mission operations.
Method: Annual agency disclosure of identified AI use cases.
Denominator: NASA use cases included under the federal inventory definition in each reporting year.
why_it_matters: Which records connect compute, data, evaluation, and program support to institutional adoption, reproduced scientific work, and measured research outcomes? This record supplies one bounded part of that evidence chain; it is not a substitute for the pack's downstream records. This observation adds one of three time points for the nasa public ai-use inventory series and keeps its unit, denominator, period, geography, method, attribution, and series-break context attached.
ftfn_relevance: Adds one of twelve Phase 56A primary records for institutional AI and cybersecurity system performance.
Supports a within-domain time series without creating a cross-domain score.
Makes revision, denominator, and method limits visible before a direction is described.
evidence_limits: Inclusion in a Phase 65 reporting pack does not advance a Phase 64 matrix cell or establish an operating outcome.
Active-use labels do not establish comparable benefit, reliability, or safety outcomes.
The observation is bounded to United States federal civil-space program and the stated period.
The denominator is NASA use cases included under the federal inventory definition in each reporting year.
Two-point movement is not presented as a durable trend without an explicit caveat.
